output.week_summary: Three ideas are worth developing this week: how WIA helps couples understand a venue's value, why we give each Meta creative a different job, and how Carmen uses client feedback when reviewing search terms. Publish the search-language opinion first, the Meta strategy piece second, and the venue landing-page piece last with the week's sole Instagram offer CTA, DM 'ADS'. The Meta strategy idea can also anchor a standalone Tuesday email without an offer CTA. The geography check and photography wording are useful planning inputs, while the prospect's reaction to ongoing cost belongs in sales notes. No founder seeds this cycle.

angles.title: Why we'd put a venue comparison chart on the ads landing page
angles.audience: Venue owners who want their advertising to bring in couples who understand the value of their packages.
angles.core_perspective: When we plan a venue's ads landing page, we want couples to understand what they're comparing. An all-inclusive package and a venue rental include different things, and that explanation can help a couple decide whether to inquire. We look for the information owners already use in their sales conversations and consider where it belongs on the ads landing page.
angles.why_it_matters: Whitney's belief: 'People want more information before committing to a conversation.' For an owner who wants quality inquiries, the shift is toward helping couples understand the offer while they're deciding whether to reach out. This makes WIA's landing-page thinking concrete without claiming that we handle the venue's sales.
angles.wia_in_action: The venue owner described an existing comparison chart she used on her website and in follow-up. Whitney recommended including it on the ads landing page. The owner supplied the comparison; WIA identified another place where it could support a couple's decision.
angles.offer_connection: Connect this to ELEVATE's done-for-you Google and Meta ads management, strategic creative, conversion tracking, ongoing optimization and LeadLock. The landing-page recommendation shows one part of the thinking behind that paid acquisition system. Use the week's sole Instagram offer CTA: DM 'ADS'.
evidence_points: The owner explained that couples were comparing her all-inclusive package with venue rental only and did not always understand the value of the included services.
She already had a venue comparison chart and used it to explain inclusions and estimated outside costs in follow-up.
Whitney recommended including that comparison on the ads landing page.
verify_before_publishing: Review permission for an anonymized account of this call.
If showing the chart, confirm its inclusions and outside-cost estimates with the venue.
angles.why_selected: This has the clearest offer connection and a specific WIA recommendation. It shows how the team brings useful sales information into the advertising experience, rather than offering generic advice about explaining value. No implementation or booking result is needed to demonstrate the thinking.

angles.title: Why we give each venue ad a different job
angles.audience: Wedding business owners who want to understand the creative decisions behind a layered Meta campaign.
angles.core_perspective: We choose creative around what we're asking a couple to do next. Introducing a venue, inviting an inquiry and helping someone weigh their options call for different messages. That's why our Meta strategy gives each layer its own purpose and lets that purpose guide the creative.
angles.why_it_matters: Whitney's belief: 'For a wedding business, every touchpoint matters more.' The owner's question was whether the same creative could run with different targeting. This shifts the conversation toward what each ad should help a couple understand or decide, giving owners a clearer way to understand our campaign choices.
angles.wia_in_action: Whitney explained the different objectives of client attraction, conversion and warm retargeting. She connected each objective to the kind of creative it calls for, from a venue introduction to a tour invitation to a deeper explanation of why the venue may be the right fit.
angles.offer_connection: This demonstrates the strategic thinking behind WIA's Meta campaign planning. Keep it as a trust-building piece without an offer CTA.
evidence_points: The owner asked whether each layer had separate creative or whether one creative was targeted in different ways.
Whitney described client attraction as an introduction to the venue for cold audiences.
She described conversion creative as a direct request to inquire or book a tour.
She described warm retargeting as deeper content about why couples should choose the venue.
verify_before_publishing: Review permission for an anonymized account of this call.
angles.why_selected: The owner's question gives WIA a natural opening to explain a real planning decision. Its central point is creative chosen by campaign objective, which is more specific than the recently published idea about trust across touchpoints and platforms. A second treatment would repeat the same point.

angles.title: Couples can find the right photographer before they know the photography terms
angles.audience: Photographers and other wedding pros who want their ads to reach well-matched couples, even when those couples describe what they want differently.
angles.core_perspective: A couple can know what they love in your photos and describe it differently than you would. We leave room for that when reviewing search terms. Before excluding a phrase, we want to understand what happens in the inquiries and conversations behind it.
angles.why_it_matters: Whitney's belief: 'good marketing decisions start with good data.' For owners who want quality inquiries, this expands how we judge fit. The words a couple uses are one clue, and the owner's experience with those inquiries helps us decide what to do with that clue.
angles.wia_in_action: Carmen asked whether inquiries mentioning 'light and airy' went on to become clients before recommending leaving the term available for now. She also left open excluding it later if the search activity proved irrelevant.
angles.offer_connection: This shows the wedding-specific judgment WIA brings to Google Ads. Let the opinion stand without an offer CTA.
evidence_points: The photographer said 'light and airy' did not describe her style, but couples sometimes used it in inquiry forms.
She questioned whether couples always knew how to describe the photography they wanted.
Carmen asked about the booking relevance of those inquiries before making her recommendation.
Carmen recommended leaving the term available for now and revisiting it if search activity became irrelevant.
verify_before_publishing: Review permission for an anonymized account of this call; omit private booking figures.
angles.why_selected: Carmen's question is the distinctive contribution. It turns a keyword discussion into a wedding-specific opinion about how couples describe what they want, with a clear example of WIA using client knowledge to inform campaign decisions. It offers reach without blaming owners or teaching keyword basics.

internal_insights.insight: Carmen checked which market was in scope, and the photographer chose Orlando for now. The explanation about mountain imagery and different expectations came from the client. Denver remained a possible future market, not an agreed next step.
internal_insights.use: Keep Orlando as the current campaign focus in planning notes. Preserve the client's market-specific imagery insight without turning it into a universal rule that every city requires a separate landing page.

internal_insights.insight: The photographer wants candid imagery to remain central to her positioning while reassuring couples that she'll provide direction during portraits. 'Authentic, not staged' was her suggestion. The excerpt contains no WIA response or confirmed wording decision.
internal_insights.use: Use this in the creative brief to distinguish natural moments from an absence of guidance. Retrieve the team's response before building public content about how WIA reviewed or revised the promise.

internal_insights.insight: The prospect valued the system's breadth and was willing to recommend it, while questioning the ongoing cost in relation to her limited annual wedding capacity. That is a fit and investment consideration, not a rejection of the system's value. The offer being discussed is not identified in this excerpt, and no WIA diagnostic questions are shown.
internal_insights.use: Keep this in sales research and verify the offer before attaching the feedback to a product. Explore what ongoing value the prospect understood and what business goals she wanted it to support. Do not use her booking cap as a public eligibility rule or turn her reaction into advice about doubting WIA's offers.

considered_not_selected.reason: There is a useful scope check, but the market and landing-page reasoning comes from the client. The excerpt does not show enough additional WIA planning to make this as distinctive as the selected process pieces.

considered_not_selected.idea: A photographer can promise candid photos and still offer direction
considered_not_selected.reason: The client insight is strong, but there is no visible WIA response or decision. On its own, this would become advice to photographers rather than evidence of WIA's contribution.

considered_not_selected.idea: A campaign breakdown showing this venue's three Meta layers
considered_not_selected.reason: The scene explains the strategy, but it provides no launched creatives or campaign performance to break down. The selected behind-the-scenes treatment fits the evidence and avoids presenting a proposed approach as an implemented campaign.

pillar_notes.note: Use the photography search-language opinion for reach. Its authority comes from Carmen's decision process, with no offer CTA or private result.
Use the Meta creative discussion to show how WIA plans campaigns. Keep the focus on each creative's job so it adds something specific beyond recent content about trust across touchpoints.
Close with the venue comparison recommendation. It makes ELEVATE's landing-page thinking tangible and earns DM 'ADS' as the week's sole Instagram offer CTA. No audit promotion.
